title: The Chairs Never Lost

beats.text: The world's most famous stock index fired every company it started with.
Charles Dow adds twelve stock prices, divides by twelve, and gets forty point nine four.
Your giants? Leather, sugar, tobacco, gas, and a whiskey trust feeding cattle its leftover mash.
The whiskey trust is out by eighteen ninety-nine.
By twenty eighteen, the last original is gone, swapped for a drugstore chain.
Not one of the twelve is left.
This year, the Dow crossed fifty thousand.
How does a list outlive everything on it?
You see, it's like your school's football team.
Every kid in the old photo graduated, and the jersey still plays Friday.
A fading company gets benched; a rising one takes its seat.
The chairs never lost a game.

facts.claim: On May 26, 1896 Charles Dow added the prices of 12 industrial stocks, divided by 12 (a simple arithmetic average) and published 40.94
The original twelve included U.S. Leather, American Sugar, American Tobacco, Chicago Gas and Laclede Gas, and the Distilling & Cattle Feeding Company (the Whiskey Trust)
The Whiskey Trust fed the spent grain/stillage from its distilleries to cattle (hence 'Cattle Feeding')
Distilling & Cattle Feeding was dropped from the Dow in 1899
GE, the last original member, was replaced by Walgreens Boots Alliance (a drugstore chain) on June 26, 2018; no original member remains
The Dow crossed 50,000 for the first time on February 6, 2026
Components are replaced over time (30 seats since 1928); e.g. Alphabet replaced Verizon in 2026

caption:
May 26, 1896: Charles Dow added up 12 industrial stock prices, divided by 12, and got 40.94. Leather, sugar, tobacco, gas, even a whiskey trust that fed cattle its leftover mash.
One by one they were dropped. GE, the last original, left in 2018.
In February 2026 the Dow crossed 50,000 anyway.
